newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, March 11 - Vancouver, B.C. - GRAIN - 7 Vessels loading, 19 waiting, delays very dependent on grades to be loaded and are now about 3 weeks. 14 Vessels due to arrive before the end of March. Roberts Bank - COAL - 2 Vessels loading, 5 waiting, delays of 2-3 days occurring, normal bunching. 15 Vessels due before the end of March. Prince Rupert - GRAIN - 1 Vessel loading, 12 waiting, cargo for the next 3 vessels in house.

HONDURAS, March 10 - Puerto Cortes - Six vessels berthed of which 2 discharging/loading containers/general cargo, 1 discharging/loading containers/bananas, 1 discharging/loading fuel oil, 2 discharging wheat. 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 in ballast, 1 to discharge grain/soya. 19 Vessels due of which 1 passenger, 10 to discharge/load containers/general cargo, 5 to discharge/load containers/bananas. 3 To discharge (1 fuel oil, 1 explosives, 1 liquid chemicals). Puerto Cortes - Seven vessels berthed of which discharging/loading containers, 1 discharging urea, 1 discharging sbm, 1 discharging fuel oil and discharging containers/loading bananas. 5 Vessels awaiting berths of which 3 to discharge/load containers, 1 to discharge fertiliser, 1 to discharge corn. 18 Vessels due of which 4 to discharge bananas, 1 passenger vessel. 8 To load/discharge containers, 1 to discharge chemicals, 2 to discharge fuel, 1 to discharge wheat/corn, 1 to load sugar.

PANAMA, March 10 - Cristobal - 17 Vessels berthed of which 2 operating. Balboa - 17 Vessels berthed of which 2 operating. Panama Canal - Transit booking system working normally (full capacity). Position 10/3, 38 vessels due, 13 in queue, 10 booked, 37 scheduled. Conditions 9/3, actual arrivals 31, transits 35, average of booked and non-booked canal waters time 20.8 hours.

UNITED STATES, March 10 - Jersey City, NJ, Perth Amboy, NJ - No vessels. Port Newark, NJ - Five vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Two vessels in port. Bayway, NJ - One vessel in port. Cartaret, NJ - One vessel in port. All northern New Jersey ports working normally, with no congestion/delays. Baltimore, MD - Port working normally, 8 bulkers, 2 container vessels, 1 ro-ro, 2 auto vessels, 2 tankers, 2 general cargo vessels. 5 Vessels awaiting berths of which 2 to discharge sugar, 2 to discharge autos, 1 under arrest.

Hampton Roads, VA - Five general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 2 bulkers berthed loading coal, 3 vessels berthed under repair/layberth. Honolulu, HI - Honolulu harbour - 2 Container vessels, 1 tanker, 4 tugs and barges berthed. No vessels at anchorage. Barbers Point - 1 Bulk carrier, 2 barges berthed. Offport moorings - 1 Tanker.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - No congestion expected at Dundalk terminal this week. Clear Candd canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Consol Coal - Average waiting time 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities - Working normally with no congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - No vessels due at either shipyard river coal terminal or grain elevator over the next week. Jacksonville, FL - No heavy congestion at Jacksonville or Fernandina Beach. Miami, FL - No congestion at container berths, gantry berths or ro-ro berths, which are available all week. Dredging operations will close the channel near the government cut for twelve hours, one night each week, for four weeks. Closure will take place from 18.00-06.00 hrs. On March 11, 18, 25 and April 1.

New York - No congestion at anchorages, none at container or tanker terminals. Congestion in sugar terminal. Norfolk, VA - Southern Coal pier - 19 Vessels due during the week, 1 anchored waiting to load. Scheduled maintenance to No. 1 ship loading system from 8-29/4, during which time it will be out of order. Dominion terminal - 9 Vessels due, 3 anchored waiting to load. Pier IX coal terminal - 4 Vessels due during the week. Cargill - No vessels due this week. Container, general cargo, oil and bulk terminals - All working normally, with no delays. All channels open and ice-free, with prevailing depths available. International terminal - Crane no. 7 out of service until approx. 15/3, when cranes no. 6 and no. 5 will separately be taken out of service for upgrading. All upgrades expected to be finished by 30/6. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion at Camden, Wilmington or Philadelphia. No dredging/navigational problems.

Savannah, GA - Garden City terminal expecting a moderate week. Ocean terminal and east coast terminal also expect a moderate week, with no delays expected. Colonial Marine terminal's bulk clay facility expects long delays. Sugar refinery remains busy, with vessels waiting at anchor. All liquid bulk facilities working normally, with no congestion expected. Navigationa normal, but vessels may expect delays due to periods of fog.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, Cargill, public grain elevator or farmland grain elevator, Galveston. However, congestion at some oil/chemical terminals. New Orleans, LA - Seasonal rains can cause delays, especially to grain loading. River stage at 13.3 feet and expected to go up to 16.3 feet by 16/3. Crest at 17 ft. by 23/3. Normal transit times expected. Bar pilots advise that draft for Misssippi river gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 47 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt., 46 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - 11 Grain vessels in port of which 5 loading and 6 waiting. Average waiting time is 3-5 days. Coos Bay, OR - Working normally. One log vessel loading, 1 lumber vessel loading/discharging. Glenbrook nickel terminal - 1 Vessel discharging. Vessel traffic expected to increase in the coming weeks. 3 Wood-chip, 2 lumber vessels due mid-week. Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan (lb-212-214) - Moderate for March, 1-2 days waiting expected at anchor for berths. Koch Carbon (lb-211) - 3 Vessels due for March, no berthing delays expected. Kaiser (la-49) - Moderate for March (coal,petcoke), 1-2 days delay expected for berths. March looks moderate in Los Angeles, Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes.

San Francisco, CA - Stockton still operating under reduced transit draft restrictions. Max. draft to and from Stockton is 30 ft. 6 ins. At Sacramento, max. transit has been temporarily set at 24 ft. 6 ins. due to discovery of a shoal. All anchorages are clear. Delays expected at Stockton and Sacramento. Seattle, WA - Both grain elevators have backlog of vessels at anchor.
